_doc: Per-unit build config, read by tools/blender/units/*.py. Every length is in SOURCE units (the generated GLB as imported), long axis on `fwd`, `h` = height above the source's lowest vertex; measure with measure_source.py. `ends_bottom_h` [rear, front] is the bottom edge of the rear plate and the bow (0 = no bow beyond the track), which verify_glb.py keeps every body vertex above. `type_id` picks the hull box from game/battle/unit_silhouettes.gd _SPECS, which fixes the uniform scale and the muzzle. `fwd` "-y" is a source whose nose points to -Y (prep.py turns it half a turn about Z). `gear.kind` "wheels" replaces the track loop with tyres: `road` {r, h, long[]} is the axle discs in SOURCE units, `cut_lat`/`cut_r` what prep removes around them, `wheel_lat` the procedural tyre's lateral span, `hub` and `bevel` its shape; no `cut`, `track_*`, `sprocket`, `idler` or `ends_bottom_h`. `towed` marks a gun on one axle (wheels, no hull roof gun): verify_glb.py then reads the muzzle as the front-most vertex. `gun.pitch` (degrees) tilts the barrel line about its breech point (`start_long`, `axis_h`); a unit with no `gun` (engineer vehicle) gets no barrel. A towed gun's `_SET_SPECS` `barrel` is the natural reach of the source barrel (prep.py logs `source tip`, the stretch stays ~1) and the profile's last ring stops short of that tip by the ring radius x sin(pitch), so the front-most vertex (the lower point of the tilted muzzle ring) lands on the row's `barrel`; `bore` is that vertex's height. `yaw` [degrees, pivot x, pivot y] turns a skewed source in its own frame (the pivot lands on the centreline: y = 0, or x = 0 for `fwd` "y"); `fwd` "-x" is a source whose nose points to -X. `cut.keep_ahead` keeps a plough ahead of the idler out of the running-gear cut, and `end_floor_rear_only` holds only the tail plate up so the plough may reach the ground. `k` fixes the uniform scale outright (a towed gun or a plough vehicle is fitted by its real size, while its _SPECS row describes only the solid carriage or hull); `hull_long` then only picks the origin, the centre of that carriage or hull. `whole_model` makes verify_glb.py skip the hull-box checks (the row is smaller than the model). `grid_half` is the half-width of the heightfield grid in model units, for a model wider than its row. `plough` [from_long, lateral factor] stretches what stands ahead of `from_long` across the hull so a plough overhangs the tracks. `lower` [[long0, long1, lat0, lat1, h_ref, factor]] presses what stands above h_ref inside the box towards it (a folded arm laid lower). `add_boxes` also builds ground kit (a firing platform, ammunition crates, plough tines). `add_discs` [[long, lat, h0, h1, r]] builds a round platform standing on the ground (a firing base). `reach` [from_long, to_long, shift] pulls the stretch of the source between the two long coordinates out by `shift` and moves everything ahead of it rigidly (push arms at their real length). `paint.blade` {y_min (metres from the model centre), colour} paints everything ahead of y_min worn steel. `gear.road.src_r` / `src_h` are the source tyre that prep cuts away when the procedural wheel (`r`, `h`) is drawn smaller than it.

medium_tank._turret: the heavy's turret made compact: scaled toward its front (the long bustle shrinks), flatter and narrower
medium_tank._flatten: the rear deck stays one flat engine deck: stowage box and mast pressed down

tank_destroyer._layout: no turret: low front hull, a tall fixed armoured box on the rear 57 %, the gun from its front face
tank_destroyer._add_boxes: a flat rear plate closing the bay under the box overhang, flush with the hull rear, down to the fenders; two low roof boxes (sight, vent) so the box reads as armour

light_tank._turret: shrunk to read small and low from above: box in SOURCE units, base_h = top of the ring

set2_heavy_tank._layout: set 2 heavy: wide flat slab turret with a solid full-width bustle, centre at 54 % of the hull from the bow
set2_heavy_tank._scale_lat: the source is 11 % narrower than the heavy's role box: lateral axis scaled before anything else, so every lat value below is in scaled source units
set2_heavy_tank._flatten: the bustle rack's posts and the antennas pressed down to the turret roof height
set2_heavy_tank._add_boxes: solid bustle across the turret rear; full-length side skirts whose bottom covers the top third of the road wheels

set2_medium_tank._layout: set 2 medium, derived from the heavy source: the slab alone (rack left out) shortened to 0.42 of the hull, its centre 38 % from the bow, a flat engine deck behind it, no bustle
set2_medium_tank._flatten: the bustle rack and its antennas pressed down to the rear deck
set2_medium_tank._add_boxes: deck plate over the vacated turret ring; full-length side skirts whose bottom covers the top third of the road wheels

set2_tank_destroyer._layout: set 2 tank destroyer: no turret, a slab-sided box over the rear half with a cupola ring on the right, the gun from its front face; the source faces -Y and was turned 180 degrees about Z
set2_tank_destroyer._scale_lat: the source's hull is 13 % too wide for the role box once its length fills it: lateral axis squeezed first, so every lat value below is in scaled source units
set2_tank_destroyer._delete_boxes: rear overhang beyond the plate and anything standing out past the hull width (fins, corner posts)
set2_tank_destroyer._flatten: the whole box roof pressed 0.02 tile lower so the destroyer stays smaller in plan mass than the heavy; the cupola is rebuilt as a low block on the right
set2_tank_destroyer._add_boxes: flat rear plate closing the bay under the rear basket with a stowage ledge and two tow-hook blocks; cupola block; full-length side skirts whose bottom covers the top third of the road wheels

set2_light_tank._layout: set 2 light: slab-sided low hull, grille deck at the front, a small faceted turret moved to mid-hull (the source has it aft), shortest gun
set2_light_tank._squash: the source is 30 % too tall for the role: everything above the running gear pressed down so the turret roof sits near 2.0 m
set2_light_tank._flatten: antennas and sights pressed down to the roof; stowage on the vacated ring pressed to the deck
set2_light_tank._delete_boxes: the crumpled cage remains on the turret rear edge (measured on the built mesh, model L -0.12..-0.09)
set2_light_tank._add_boxes: deck plate over the vacated turret ring, a small box bustle on the turret rear; side skirts whose bottom covers the top third of the road wheels

set1_heavy_tank._layout: set 1 heavy: full-width turret 29-62 % from the bow plus a solid box bustle to 75 % (add_boxes), short flat deck behind it; hull_lat is trimmed below the measured 0.2113 so k stretches the hull 2 % longer
set1_heavy_tank._add_boxes: bustle flush with the roof; two flat ERA plates per turret cheek; a rear plate with two drums on it

set1_medium_tank._layout: set 1 medium: low dome turret centred 36 % from the bow, no bustle, flat engine deck over the rear half; the hull is stretched at the rear by a plate (add_boxes) because the source hull is stubbier than the box

set1_tank_destroyer._layout: set 1 tank destroyer: no turret; low bare front deck, a fixed armoured box over the rear 57 % that starts 43 % from the bow and is carried back by one box (add_boxes) so its rear face is flush with the lengthened hull; the gun leaves its front face

set1_light_tank._layout: set 1 light: long low slab hull with a shallow glacis, a small low dome turret moved forward to mid-hull (about 49 % from the bow) and flattened to keep the top under 2 m; the barrel is stretched to the spec length

set1_engineer_vehicle._layout: hull stretched 0.129 behind the turret ring to 6.8 m (reach), blade squeezed up to 0.26 m from the bow; source cab removed above the stowed boom and replaced by an off-centre box cab; boom lowered onto the deck and ending in a flat claw
